summary: Edwin Arnold was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at King's College London and Oxford, served as schoolmaster at King Edward's School, Principal at Deccan College, Fellow at the University of Mumbai, and visiting lecturer at Keio.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Trinity College Dublin, he served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and as Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (attested 1889).

Edwin Francis Bryant is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate from Columbia University in 1997, taught at Harvard University (~1998–2003), and became Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University around 2003.

Edwin Gerow was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College (~1978–2006) and Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1987–1999).

Edwin Norris worked in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the East India Company, the Foreign Office, and the Royal Asiatic Society, where he was assistant secretary and later Assistant-Honorary Secretary and Honorary Librarian.

Edwin Whitfield Fay was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Rhodes College, Johns Hopkins, and Leipzig, and held posts at Michigan, Washington and Lee University, and the University of Texas at Austin as professor of Latin.

Egaku Mayeda was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno, he later served as professor at Tokai Gakuen Junior College, Meijo University, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Egil Asprem is a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology and the University of Amsterdam, and held posts at NTNU (2013), UC Santa Barbara (2013), and Stockholm University (2016).

Eido Shimano was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozō, and Soen Nakagawa, attended the University of Hawaiʻi, and served as abbot at the Zen Studies Society and master at New York Zendo Shobo-ji.

Eiichi Chino was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Harushige Takatsu. He held academic posts at Wako University (~1966–1969), Tokyo University of Education (~1969–1974), and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1974–1995).

Eiichi Imoto was an Iranian/Central Asian and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1953) and held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1994) and Momoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001).

Eiichi Makino was a scholar of philosophy and law. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903), he held posts there (~1903–1938), as well as at Kyushu University, Tohoku University, Chuo University (~1949), and Shiraume Gakuen Junior College (~1953–1968).
Eiichi Otani is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University from around 1987 to 1996 and served as dean and professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University around 2002.

Eiichi Yamaguchi is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He completed graduate studies at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990) and subsequently served there as a research assistant (attested 1991).
Eiin Yasuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He was a disciple of Gyoin Hashimoto and completed his studies at Ryukoku University around 1957–1961.
Eiju Fukushima is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and religious studies. Fukushima is attested in 2026 as a faculty member at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

Eiki Hoshino is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University (~1962–1970) and later served there as Professor in the Faculty of Humanities and Director (~1981–2013).
Eiko Okukaze is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2010) and later served as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

Eileen Power was a historian who studied at Girton College and the University of Paris. She held academic appointments at the London School of Economics (~1921–1940) and the University of London (~1931–1940).

Einar Thomassen is a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Bergen and the University of St Andrews, later holding posts at the University of Oslo (~1986–1993) and Bergen (~1993–2021).
